spans.s:
ज्वर् ज्वर्, cl. 1. P. ज्वरति, जज्वार, ज्वरि-
ष्यति, अज्वारीत्, ज्वरितुम्, to be feverish,
to be hot with fever or passion, to be diseased &c.:
Caus. P. ज्वरयति, -यितुम्, to make feverish: Desid.
जिज्वरिषति: Intens. जाज्वर्यते, जाजूर्ति; [cf. Lat.
a-ger; Hib. gurt, ‘pain, trouble, fierceness;’ Germ.
schwer; Old Germ. swâr, swâri; Germ. quâlen ?].
ज्वर्; add — connected with rt. ज्वल्.

ज्वर, अस्, m. fever of different kinds (called after
the different doṣas or humors of the body which
are supposed to be affected by them; fever is called
the leader and king of all diseases); fever of the
soul, mental pain, affliction, grief, trouble, sorrow,
distress; (आ), f. fever; (अस्, आ, अम्), heated, raging
(with fever, passion, &c.), excited, inflamed.
—ज्वर-
घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, febrifuge, anti-febrile, dispelling
fever or ague; (अस्), m. or according to some (ई), f.
the plant Cocculus Cordifolius, = गुडूची; the plant
Chenopodium Album, = वास्तूक.
—ज्वर-चिकित्सा,
f. medical treatment of fever.
—ज्वर-नाशक, अस्,
आ, अम्, febrifuge.
—ज्वर-निर्णय, अस्, m., N. of
a medical work.
—ज्वर-प्रतीकार, अस्, m. cure
of fever.
—ज्वर-हन्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, febrifuge;
(त्री), f. the plant Rubia Munjista.
—ज्वराग्नि (˚र-
अग्˚), इस्, m. feverish heat, the hot paroxysm in
fever.
—ज्वराङ्कुश (˚र-अङ्˚), अस्, m. a febrifuge;
[]
the plant Andropogon Jvarancusa; title of a work
on medicine.
—ज्वराङ्गी (˚र-अङ्˚), f., N. of a
plant, = भद्र-दन्तिका.
—ज्वरान्तक (˚र-अन्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, febrifuge, dispelling fever; (अस्), m.
the plant Cathartocarpus Fistula; a kind of Nimba
growing in Nepal.
—ज्वरान्वित (˚र-अन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
suffering from fever or ague.
—ज्वरापह (˚र-अप्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, febrifuge; (आ), f. a febrifuge, the plant
Medicago Esculenta, = विल्ल-पत्त्री (?).

ज्वरित, अस्, आ, अम्, or ज्वरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, febrile,
feverish, affected with fever.

ज्वल् ज्वल्, cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) ज्वलति,
-ते, जज्वाल, ज्वलिष्यति, अज्वालीत्, ज्वलि-
तुम्, to burn brightly, blaze, flame, glow, shine; to
burn (as a wound); to be ardent: Caus. P. ज्वाल-
यति and ज्वलयति, -यितुम्, to set on fire, light,
kindle, make radiant, illuminate: Desid. जिज्वलि-
षति: Intens. जाज्वल्यते, जाज्वल्ति, to flame vio-
lently, shine strongly, be brilliant; [cf. Hib. gual-
laim, ‘I blacken, burn;’ gual, ‘coal, coals, fire:’
Germ. Kohle: Old Germ. colo: Eng. coal: Lith.
swelù: Old Germ. wallu, walm, wâli.]

ज्वल, अस्, आ, अम्, flaming, blazing, shining, bril-
liant; (अस्), m. flame, blaze, light.
—ज्वल-मुखी,
f., N. of a tutelary deity in the family of Lomaśa;
[cf. ज्वाला-मुखी.]
—ज्वलानन (˚ल-आन्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, having the face flaming.
—ज्वला-रासभका-
मय, अस्, m. = जाल-गर्दभ.

ज्वाल, अस्, ई, अम्, burning, blazing; (अस्), m. light,
flame, a torch; (आ), f. a blaze, flame, illumination;
burnt rice; N. of a daughter of Takṣaka and wife
of Ṛkṣa; [cf. Hib. gual, ‘coal.’]
—ज्वाला-खर-
गद and ज्वाला-गर्दभक, अस्, m. = जाल-गर्द-
भ.
—ज्वालाग्नि (˚ल-अग्˚), इस्, m. blazing fire, flame.
—ज्वाला-जिह्व, अस्, m. ‘flame-tongued,’ N. of fire;
N. of an attendant of Skanda; of Śiva; of a Dānava.
—ज्वाला-ध्वज, अस्, m. ‘flame-marked,’ fire.
—ज्वा-
ला-मुख, अस्, m. ‘flame-mouthed,’ a class of demons;
(ई), f. a volcano; any place where subterranean fire
or inflammable gas breaks forth, such places being
held sacred by the Hindūs as indicating the presence
of a form of Durgā; (a celebrated Jvālā-mukhī exists
in the hills north-east of the Pañjāb to which pilgrim-
ages are made; the soil abounds with carburetted
hydrogen gas which takes fire upon coming in con-
tact with the external air. According to the legend,
the flame proceeds from the fire which the wife of
Śiva created and in which she burned herself. Śiva
finding that this flame was about to consume the
world, buried it in the hollow of the mountain.
According to another legend, the tongue of Pārvatī
fell at this place. There is a similar volcanic region
in Chinese Tartary where fire is produced by digging
into the earth.)
—ज्वाला-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘flame-liṅga,’
N. of a temple of Śiva.
—ज्वाला-वक्त्र, अस्, m. ‘flame-
mouthed,’ N. of an attendant of Śiva.
—ज्वालेश्वर
(˚ल-ईश्˚), N. of a Tīrtha.
ज्वलका, f. a large flame or blaze.

ज्वलत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, burning, blazing; shining,
radiant, brilliant.
—ज्वलन्-मणि, इस्, इस्, इ, blazing
with jewels; (इस्), m. a brilliant gem.

ज्वलन, अस्, आ, अम्, inflammable, combustible,
flaming, shining; (अस्), m. fire; a N. of the numeral 3;
corrosive alkali; the plant Plumbago Zeylanica; (आ), f.,
N. of a daughter of Takṣaka and wife of Ṛceyu [cf.
ज्वाला]; (अम्), n. burning, blazing.
—ज्वलनाश्मन्
(˚न-अश्˚), आ, m. the sun-stone; [cf. सूर्य-कान्त.]
ज्वलनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, fit to be burnt, combustible.

ज्वलयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, kindling, burning, illu-
mining, blazing, radiant.

ज्वलित, अस्, आ, अम्, kindled, burnt, blazing, flam-
ing; (तृणेषु ज्वलितं त्वया, you have lighted a
fire in the grass, i. e. you have had easy work.)
—ज्वलित-नयन, अस्, आ, अम्, fiery-eyed, looking
angrily or fiercely; also ज्वलित-चक्षुस्, ज्वलित-
नेत्र, &c.
—ज्वलितानन (˚त-आन्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
having the face flaming.

ज्वलिन्, ई, इनी, इ, burning, flaming, shining; (इनी),
f. the plant Sanseviera Zeylanica, = मूर्वा.

ज्वालिन्, ई, इनी, इ, flaming, blazing; (इनी), f. mystical
name of the letter व्.
